description: Service mesh decomposed. The sidecar proxy injected next to each microservice. Envoy as the dominant data plane; Istio + Linkerd as control planes. mTLS for service-to-service authentication. Traffic policies: retries, timeouts, circuit breakers, rate limiting. Observability: metrics, traces, logs at the sidecar. Sidecar pattern's costs (latency, complexity) vs benefits (uniform cross-service policy).

sub_mechanisms.name: sidecar_proxy
sub_mechanisms.definition: Envoy (or similar) deployed as a container next to each service. All inbound + outbound traffic flows through the sidecar.
sub_mechanisms.why: Externalises cross-cutting concerns (mTLS, retries, observability). Service code stays simple; sidecar handles network policy. Pod / VM contains both processes; they communicate via localhost.

sub_mechanisms.name: control_plane
sub_mechanisms.definition: Central system (Istiod, Linkerd's destination service) that pushes configuration to all sidecars: routing rules, mTLS certificates, observability targets.
sub_mechanisms.why: Distributed sidecars need consistent policy. Control plane is the single source of truth. Updates propagate to sidecars via xDS (Envoy's discovery protocol).

sub_mechanisms.name: xDS_protocol
sub_mechanisms.definition: Envoy's discovery API: clusters (CDS), endpoints (EDS), listeners (LDS), routes (RDS), secrets (SDS). gRPC streams of config updates.
sub_mechanisms.why: Push-based config: control plane pushes changes; sidecars apply them. Lets routing change without sidecar restart. The de facto standard data plane interface for service meshes.

sub_mechanisms.name: mTLS_between_services
sub_mechanisms.definition: Mutual TLS: both client + server present certificates. Each service has an identity certificate; sidecars enforce that callers are authenticated.
sub_mechanisms.why: Zero-trust networking: no implicit trust based on network location. Every call authenticated cryptographically. Certificate rotation handled by sidecar automatically.

sub_mechanisms.name: service_identity
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each workload has a cryptographic identity (SPIFFE ID). Embedded in the certificate the sidecar presents.
sub_mechanisms.why: Authorisation based on identity, not IP. 'service-A can call service-B' rather than 'allow IP X to talk to IP Y'. Survives pod restarts + IP changes.

sub_mechanisms.name: circuit_breaker
sub_mechanisms.definition: Sidecar tracks errors / latency to each destination. When a threshold is crossed, fails fast (returns error without trying) until destination recovers.
sub_mechanisms.why: Prevents cascading failure. A failing service overwhelms its callers if they keep retrying; circuit breaker cuts that off. Standard pattern from Netflix's Hystrix.

sub_mechanisms.name: retry_with_budget
sub_mechanisms.definition: Sidecar retries failed requests up to a configured count. Often with budget: max retries per N requests, preventing retry storms.
sub_mechanisms.why: Transient failures (transient TCP RSTs, momentary 503s) often succeed on retry. Bounded budget prevents amplification during real outages — retrying a failed service in a loop makes it worse.

sub_mechanisms.name: outlier_detection
sub_mechanisms.definition: Sidecar tracks per-endpoint health. Endpoints with high error rates are temporarily ejected from the load-balancing pool.
sub_mechanisms.why: Active health checking from the data plane. A bad pod (memory leak, slow restart) is detected by behaviour, not just liveness probes. Self-healing routing.

sub_mechanisms.name: canary_deployment_routing
sub_mechanisms.definition: Sidecar routes a percentage of traffic to a new version of a service. Gradually increases as the new version proves healthy.
sub_mechanisms.why: Risk-mitigated rollouts. 1% canary catches bugs without blast radius. Full deployment only after metrics look good. Service mesh implements this without per-service code.

sub_mechanisms.name: distributed_tracing_injection
sub_mechanisms.definition: Sidecar adds trace headers (X-B3-TraceId or W3C TraceContext) to outgoing requests. Trace IDs flow through the whole call graph.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without trace injection, distributed traces would require each service to participate. Sidecar handles it transparently — applications don't need to be trace-aware.

sub_mechanisms.name: metrics_emission
sub_mechanisms.definition: Sidecar emits per-request metrics: latency, status code, retries, mTLS handshake outcomes. To Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, etc.
sub_mechanisms.why: Uniform metrics across all services without per-service code. RED metrics (Rate, Errors, Duration) automatically computed. Standard dashboards work for any service.

sub_mechanisms.name: ambient_mode_layer4_proxy
sub_mechanisms.definition: Newer pattern (Istio Ambient): split sidecar into per-node L4 proxy + per-namespace L7 proxy. Reduces per-pod overhead.
sub_mechanisms.why: Per-pod sidecar pays 1-2 hops latency per request + duplicates memory. Per-node L4 is shared; L7 only for namespaces that need it. Trade-off: less isolation, but lower overhead at scale.

derivation_rules.name: sidecar_externalises_cross_cutting_concerns
if: the sidecar handles auth / retries / observability
then: application code stays free of those concerns
derivation_rules.why: Without sidecar, each microservice reimplements mTLS, retries, tracing, rate limits. Service mesh handles them uniformly. Hundreds of services × multiple concerns = orders of magnitude code reduction + consistency.

derivation_rules.name: control_plane_centralises_policy
then: changes propagate uniformly to all sidecars
derivation_rules.why: Distributed enforcement (sidecars) with central definition (control plane). Update a rule once; xDS pushes to all sidecars. Without central plane, each service operator would have to apply policies individually.

derivation_rules.name: mTLS_enables_zero_trust
then: network location no longer determines trust
derivation_rules.why: Pre-mesh model: 'trust traffic from inside the firewall'. Failed when attackers got inside. mTLS authenticates each call individually — attacker needs the service's private key, not just network access. Zero-trust pattern.

derivation_rules.name: circuit_breaker_prevents_cascading_failure
then: circuit breaker prevents callers from amplifying the failure
derivation_rules.why: Without circuit breakers, every caller retries the failing service. Retries pile up; failing service can't recover; callers cascade their own failures. Circuit breaker stops the retry storm — callers fail fast, downstream can recover.

derivation_rules.name: sidecar_latency_compounds_per_hop
if: each microservice has a sidecar adding 1-2ms
then: multi-hop call paths accumulate sidecar latency
derivation_rules.why: A 5-hop microservice path adds 5-10ms of sidecar overhead. For latency-sensitive applications, this matters. Trade-off: developer productivity vs hop latency. Ambient mode (L4-only nodes) reduces but doesn't eliminate this.
